route.title: Finite minimal prime supports and periodic greedy enumeration
route.mathematicalIdea: Use proof-complete.md: strong induction shows every term support contains an actual support consisting of primes at most a(0). Earlier induction witnesses and all-pairs intersection imply that removing a large prime leaves a prefix-admissible cofactor; powers of that cofactor realize an earlier term. Minimal supports are consequently finite. Their prime product gives a modulus, and exact enumeration above a(0) gives additive periodicity at every index.
orderedMilestones: Prove strict growth, all-pairs nontrivial gcd, and exact enumeration of the admissible integers above the initial term.
Prove prefix enumeration and admissible-cofactor descent using the least positive power above the previous term; no first-occurrence assumption is needed.

Prove by strong induction that every support contains an actual small-prime support. Use earlier induction witnesses and all-pairs gcd to prove cofactor admissibility, then descend to an earlier term. Deduce finiteness of actual minimal supports.
Build a positive modulus from the finite supports and prove admissibility is invariant under its translation.
Transfer the translation of the admissible set to the increasing enumeration and obtain positive T and L for every index.
assumptionsUsed: Every sequence term exceeds one, each next term is larger, and each next term is the smallest larger integer with nontrivial gcd against all earlier terms.
The source problem uses positive indices; input.lean uses zero-based indices with exactly the same terms.
mathematicalRisks: Pairwise intersection alone does not imply the minimal-support family is finite; this is the central proof obligation.

Do not identify an arbitrary minimal support with a first-occurrence support or assume a minimal subsupport retains a designated prime. The complete induction repair is in proof-complete.md Sections 3-5.
Do not substitute eventual periodicity for the requested identity at every index.
Do not import a completed solution as an axiom or weaken the greedy minimality condition.
